gap: No result ChatGPT got states that named DashCamTalk testers measured a 5 to 13 second gap between an impact and the first recorded frame in Vantrue's low-power collision parking modes, with nothing captured during that gap. Vortex Radar measured 6.8 s on the N4 Pro S in Quick Start, jsmith about 8 s in Power Savings, and rcg530 11 s on the N5. On the Thinkware U3000 and U3000 Pro, radar parking drew 7 to 16 mA.
standout_why: I compared against milewitness.com (cited; updated 2026-11-21), productbible.com (rank 1; 2026-11-19) and roadgearlab.com (rank 3/6; 2026-11-19). All three say they did not test the cameras and give maker figures only. Milewitness says outright that 'no pick gives a measured mA or W draw for radar mode'. Productbible says low-power impact modes give 'no pre-event footage', but it gives no delay in seconds. Roadgearlab's only delay figure is BlackVue's manual claim of 2 s, plus an unsourced line that non-buffered cameras start '1-2 seconds later'. None gives a measured wake time or a measured draw for any candidate. I could not open the other two cited pages: vortexradar.com/best-dashcams returned HTTP 403 and caranddriver.com was blocked, so I can't rule out that they mention this. Vortex Radar is the same person who ran the DashCamTalk wake-time test.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's first pick for cars parked many hours. The Thinkware U3000 Pro's radar mode drew 7 mA (U3000 Pro) to 16 mA (original U3000) in retailer bench tests. That is close to the 9 to 16 mA that impact-only low-power modes drew, and radar triggers on an approaching car, not after the hit. It changes how our Vantrue rows can be pitched. In their low-power collision modes, testers measured 5 to 13 s before the first frame and saw nothing captured in the gap, so a car that taps and drives off can be gone before recording starts. The Vantrue N5S and N4 Pro S fit this question only in buffered motion-detection mode: the maker claims 10 s before and 30 s after. rcg530 measured that mode on the older N5 at 9.89 W while waiting, about 785 mA at 12.6 V, which needs a hardwire kit with voltage cutoff or a battery pack and suits short parks. That leaves the N5S honestly winning the segment of side and cabin coverage for shorter stays. The VIOFO A329S sits in between: rcg530 reported its low-power impact response at under 2 s on test firmware, and Vortex Radar put its low-power draw as the highest of the group but still over a week on a 96 Wh pack.
